newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks end up in bullish session.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks end up in bullish session.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed higher on a generally bullish mood that mostly ignored volatility on Wall Street, traders said.
The Bovespa index of 49 most-active stocks closed up 1.55 percent at 9565. Volume was strong at 671 million reais ($639 million).

The local market got a boost from a rumor in New York that Standard & Poor's Corp would upgrade Brazil's sovereign risk rating. S&P's president said Tuesday in Sao Paulo that the rating agency would review its current B-plus rating on Brazil sometime next month.
Telebras benefitted most from the rumor, with preferred common shares gaining 2.34 percent at 111.30.

CVRD shares, however, suffered on continued speculation about the government's minimum price of 10.3 billion reais. Preferred shares fell 1.67 percent to close at 26.50 and common shares were off 0.32 percent at 31.60.
"People are wondering what the premium will be when it is sold. Will it be 30 percent higher than the minimum price or what? I think CVRD will be volatile until it is auctioned," said one trader.

The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index (IEE) firmed 0.22 percent to close at 2647. The index, which includes the nine most liquid power stocks, was restrained by only modest gains in state-owned power company Eletrobras. Eletrobras preferred shares rose just 0.4 percent to close at 507.
